judgment.reason: The premises establish a chain of conditionals connecting Ada's copper ribbon through to an ivory ribbon, combined with an explicit denial of the ivory ribbon. Using classical modus tollens backward: (1) p22 states Ada does NOT wear an ivory ribbon; (2) p26 (teal ribbon → ivory ribbon) by modus tollens implies Ada does NOT wear a teal ribbon; (3) p17 (cobalt badge → teal ribbon) implies Ada does NOT wear a cobalt badge; (4) p0 (scarlet scarf → cobalt badge) implies Ada does NOT wear a scarlet scarf; (5) p30 (copper ribbon → scarlet scarf) implies Ada does NOT wear a copper ribbon. Each link uses identical propositions at consequent-to-antecedent junctions. The Ben register premises (p1–p29 except p0, p17, p22, p26, p30) establish only Ben's record-keeping and do not connect to Ada's attire. The False argument's objection that propositions "cross categories" (ribbon→scarf→badge) misunderstands classical logic: a conditional has no category requirement and links only two propositions regardless of subject matter. The chain is valid, and the query follows necessarily from the premises.
